pr_title: Provide new client and server websocket handshake exceptions
pr_body:
Motivation:

At the moment we have only one base `WebSocketHandshakeException` for handling WebSocket upgrade issues.
Unfortunately, this message contains only a string message about the cause of the failure, which is inconvenient in handling.

Modification:

Provide new `WebSocketClientHandshakeException` with `HttpResponse` field  and `WebSocketServerHandshakeException` with `HttpRequest` field both of them without content for avoid reference counting 
problems. 

Result:

More information for more flexible handling.

Fixes #10277 #4528 #10639.

issue_context.title: [Improvement] Add Http status as a separate field in exception on not 101 HTTP response code during web socket handshake
issue_context.body:
### Reason
In my project (built on top of Spring Cloud Gateway https://github.com/spring-cloud/spring-cloud-gateway) to be able to properly proxy HTTP response (on not 101 Http response code) from the backend server to the client, I need to extract actual Http Status code. For now, it could be done only by parsing the exception's message.
To simplify such use cases I'd like to introduce the sub-class of the WebSocketHandshakeException and enrich it with actual Http status to avoid extra string parsing.
### Expected behavior
In the case of the wrong Http Status during Handshake throw WrongStatusWebSocketHandshakeException (for example) with Http status as an exception field
### Actual behavior
Actual Http status code could be only obtained by parsing exception's message of the WebSocketHandshakeException.
### Steps to reproduce
Try to establish a web-socket  connection with a server which returns not 101 HttpStatus code
### Minimal yet complete reproducer code (or URL to code)
I can create a reproducible  sample, but it seems obvious from the code
https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/websocketx/WebSocketClientHandshaker13.java#L274
(same for other Handshaker implementations ).

I omitted versions since they are not relevant in this case.
comments: So, what if we extend the current exception to `ClientWebSocketHandshakeException` and add `HttpResponse` field and `ServerWebSocketHandshakeException` with `HttpRequest` and provide additional hint `AbortingType` like INVALID_RESPONSE_STATUS, INVALID_CONNECTION_HEADER,... and other by https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455#section-4.2.2. WDYT @normanmaurer, @slandelle ?
@amizurov I am a bit hesitant as this may also put the burden of reference counting on the user.

> @amizurov I am a bit hesitant as this may also put the burden of reference counting on the user.

I mean only `DefaultHttpResponse` and `DefaultHttpRequest` without body, in most of case it will be enough.

From my perspective it will be sufficient just to bypass a separate field in exception the information which is already present in it's exception message, just to avoid parsing strings.
But I agree with @amizurov  that whole meta-information (like headers) will cover more use cases.
From other perspective I don't find similar tickets here, and not sure whether someone need any information, which is not provided in message.
In any case I can contribute this improvement if it will be welcomed.
WDYT @normanmaurer  ?

Hi, guys added some related links according this discussion
 
- #4528 (i think this is first mention about problem)

- https://github.com/spring-cloud/spring-cloud-gateway/issues/1884 (similar to our case)

review_comments: assert !(httpRequest instanceof ReferenceCounted); and make constructors package private for now
Hmm, we create our own `DefaultHttpResponse` in constructor, we don't set given response directly.
Hmm what kind of benefit for package-private constructors?, maybe user want to create it own exception `Server` or `Client` exception and handle it in common manner.
I was thinking of make it more safe in terms of not pass in `ReferenceCounted` objects. That said as you mention before we copy it anyway so not a big deal

I wonder if it would be better to expose the protocol, status and headers directly here. This would make it clear that this `HttpResponse` is never a `FullHttpResponse` and so not needs to be released. WDYT ?

I thought about this, but we have situations when an exception occurs before receiving a response and we do not have this data and all fields will be null, which is inconvenient (need to check before use) or we can throw the different type of exceptions with response data and  without it.
got it... maybe we should just add to the java docs that this will never be `ReferenceCounted` and so no special treatment is needed.
Make sense, even that WebSocket Handshake request/response in theory should not contain payload, but this is not explicitly prohibited by the RFC 😲
